bank_access: Traditional banks (SEB, Swedbank, Luminor) require in-person KYC and usually a residence permit. Partially online options exist via SEB's remote application and fintechs (Revolut, Paysera, Wise) opening accounts with just a passport.
A cuenta no residente requires a NIE first and an in-person branch visit for KYC and signature. Fully remote opening is not offered by major Spanish banks (BBVA, Santander) for a foreign foundation.

A NIF (tax number) is a hard prerequisite. Many banks require an in-person KYC branch visit; a NIF can be obtained remotely via a Portuguese fiscal representative, and some banks allow online onboarding.

In-person branch visit is mandatory. A codice fiscale (tax code) and physical identity verification are required by Italian banks; there is no remote onboarding pathway for a foreign fondazione account.

Effectively blocked for a remote foreign founder. The IOR (Vatican Bank) serves only Catholic institutions (dioceses, religious orders) as external clients and requires in-person, institutional due diligence.

Remote is possible: Bank of Israel rules permit video KYC. Bank Hapoalim's and Leumi's international desks let non-residents complete onboarding remotely (email + video), though not all branches offer this.
In-person visit to a Jordanian bank (e.g. Arab Bank, CBJ) is mandatory for KYC. A local address/presence is effectively required for a foreign charitable entity; no remote onboarding exists.
In-person KYC at a Lebanese bank is required. A local financial representative is common. Some banks accept a power of attorney, but a physical presence for the initial meeting is the standard.

Effectively blocked: international sanctions and strict Central Bank of Syria rules restrict foreign access. Local in-person presence and a Syrian counterparty are required; remote onboarding is unavailable.

Local in-person presence at an Iraqi bank (e.g. Bank of Baghdad, FIB) is required. A local representative/agent is typically needed; CBI AML rules mandate physical identity verification for foreign founders.

Requires a MISA licence, commercial registration, and an in-person visit to a SAMA-regulated bank. A local sponsor/agent is typically needed; fully remote onboarding is not available to a foreign founder.
A local in-person visit to a Kuwaiti bank is mandatory. A local Kuwaiti representative/sponsor is typically required for a foreign charitable entity; remote onboarding is not available.
In-person branch visit is mandatory. Qatari banks (QNB, QIIB, Dukhan) require a QID and physical presence at opening; a local partner/agent is usually needed for a foreign charitable institution.

An in-person meeting is nearly always required at the bank (Emirates NBD, ADCB, FAB). A local signatory with a UAE residence visa is usually required; fully digital onboarding is generally unavailable to non-residents.
An in-person visit to an Omani bank is required. A local representative/partner is typically needed; Central Bank of Oman AML rules mandate physical identity verification for a foreign founder.
An in-person branch visit is mandatory for account opening. A local representative is typically required for a foreign NGO; CBBA AML rules apply and remote onboarding is not available.
Effectively blocked for a remote founder: instability, sanctions, and Central Bank of Yemen rules require local in-person presence. A Yemeni representative is essential; no remote onboarding exists.
Local in-person presence at a Palestinian bank (e.g. PAB, NBL Bank) is required. A local agent is typically needed; Central Bank of Palestine AML rules mandate physical identity verification.

A 2024 CBE circular permits non-resident foreigners to open accounts subject to AML checks. An in-person visit, passport, and proof of an Egyptian address are required; a local representative is helpful.

Local in-person presence is required. A Sudanese agent/representative is essential given instability and sanctions; Bank of Sudan AML rules mandate physical verification. Remote onboarding is not available.
